To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new procedure, called ADeLE, for meta-analyzing individual data across multiple studies in the high dimensional sparse regression setting.

we propose a novel integrative analysis method that can be used for aggregating and debiasing local estimators to obtain a more accurate estimate in the high dimensional heterogeneous setting, and that the ADeLE method is shown to be equivalent in performance to an ideal method that shares all individual data across all studies.
we proposed an individual data protected integrative regression procedure that aggregates and debiases local estimators, and the ADeLE achieves the minimax rate in estimation and prediction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel integrative procedure that can be applied to high dimensional heterogeneous data without sharing individual data across multiple studies.
the fundamental question of how to perform integrative analysis in high-dimensional heterogeneous data without sharing individual data.
the problem of integrative analysis of multiple studies with high dimensional heterogeneous data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ADeLE is an effective and powerful procedure for integrative analysis of high dimensional heterogeneous data.
the ADeLE method provides a novel approach for meta-analysis of multiple heterogeneous studies in the high dimensional sparse regression setting, which can be applied to real-world data analysis.

the ADeLE is an effective procedure for integrating multiple heterogeneous studies in the presence of high dimensional covariates, without sharing individual level data across studies, which can be used to derive accurate phenotyping algorithms for clinical applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ADeLE is an effective and privacy preserving procedure that enables integrative analysis of high dimensional heterogeneous data.
the ADeLE approach provides a powerful framework for integrative analysis of multiple studies with individual data protection and high-dimensional sparse linear models.
the ADeLE method can achieve the best of both worlds, namely, protecting privacy and achieving high prediction accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
individual level data can be effectively protected and aggregated for integrative analysis, while the statistical efficiency loss incurred by the data aggregation is negligible.
individual data can be protected in a meta-analytical study without losing the power of the study.
individual data protection is not necessarily a hindrance for data integration.
